privacy_ondevice_title: Your learning data stays on your device
privacy_ondevice_body: Your progress, reviews and settings are stored only on this device, in your browser's own storage (IndexedDB). FrenchPath has no accounts, no analytics, no ads and no crash reporting. We do not receive anything you do in the app.
privacy_backups_body: A backup or an encrypted sync file is created only when you choose to make one. It goes wherever you save or share it. FrenchPath does not send it anywhere.
privacy_mic_body: The microphone is used only in speaking exercises, and only after you tap to record. Your voice is processed on your device. It is never uploaded and never saved: a recording is kept in memory only so you can play it back or get your score, and is then discarded.
privacy_downloads_body: Two features contact FrenchPath's own server, and only when you use them: downloading the speaking pack (the speech model that runs on your device) and the update check, which you can switch on in Settings. Like any web request, these reveal your device's IP address to the server that hosts the app. Apart from loading the app's own pages and files, FrenchPath makes no other network requests.
privacy_tts_body: Text-to-speech uses the voices on your device, and FrenchPath lists voices that run on your device first. On some browsers a voice may be provided by the browser's vendor and work over the network.
privacy_hosting_body: When you load FrenchPath on the web, the company that hosts it keeps standard server logs, such as your IP address, the time and the file requested.
privacy_delete_body: Settings → Reset removes everything FrenchPath stored on this device: progress, settings, the downloaded speaking pack and offline copies of the app. You can also clear this site's data in your browser settings.
privacy_contact_body: Use “Report a problem or suggest an idea” in Settings → About. It opens our GitHub issues page, where posts are public, so please do not include personal information. Links that leave FrenchPath (feedback, the releases page) open GitHub, which has its own privacy policy.
